title: The Nature of God's Enemies and the Deception of the Tongue
english: They shall be written: all things happening to them in all things, and all darkness, and all grief, and pain, and the sighing happening from the feet, but in a bright day they shall shine forth like the sun in the kingdom of their own Father. For it is said, 'They shall be made as the Day' (Ps 139:16), so that they are no longer in the darkness of their creation, being sown in corruption and in dishonor, but in light and in a day standing together, being raised in incorruption and glory.

But since they are not made such as the day, and since all things happening in all things are written in the book of God, God will be in them, and there is no one among them of the evil ones or worthy of being despised. Perhaps the multitude and the 'who' and the 'no one' will vanish; for because of a great perfection and for the sake of oneness and identity, having restored the number, there shall no longer exist a 'who' or a 'no one' among them, having understood all things into the unity of the Spirit. The 'who' and the 'no one' shall no longer be among them.

A scripture is brought forward: 'My unformed eyes saw you' (Ps 139:16). And let this itself be understood likewise: 'You understood my thoughts from afar,' instead of 'the unformed of my thoughts'; before anything is accomplished, your eyes, seeing all hidden things, are full. And the Gospels are full of such things. They are friends of God, having come to be from faith and virtue. For it is said concerning Abraham: 'Abraham believed God, and it was counted to him for righteousness, and he was called a friend of God' (Gen 15:6); and concerning Moses it says: 'God spoke to him mouth to mouth, face to face, as if one were speaking to his own friend' (Exod 33:11). But even the greatest of the prophets has not become such a friend of God. And toward the apostles, indeed (they possess this friendship), Jesus says: 'I say to you, my friends' (John 15:15).

And these rulers, receiving authority from the King Christ over more than ten cities or more than five cities, are very strong as they co-reign with Christ. And it is said also by another meaning: their rule is strong because the reasons for it are friends of God. For those who are highly honored, friends of God, through a multitude of contemplations and good activities which they have, shall be multiplied beyond the immaterial, that is, beyond the sensible and the bodily. For since the companions of the material [things] regarding the immaterial [are] under this as the foundation of the house...

Their path, having fallen easily upon this, is established or fortified under this; which carries a symbol: the Egyptian, having been struck down by Moses after being seized by error, is necessarily taking a super-cosmic disposition, being worthy to be numbered by God despite the error (Ps 138:21-22). Regarding the same, it is to accept and honor the friends of God and to hate those who hate him, and to count as enemies the impious and those who think foolishly concerning God. For how are those who turn the deceived away from the truth not enemies of God, since God wills all men to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth (1 Tim 2:4)? And perfect hatred exists against such people, not for the sake of another, but because one hates them as enemies of God. And just as someone has perfect love toward the good, not for the sake of another but desiring it for its own sake, so the one hating those diverse from God does so not for the sake of another but because they are enemies of God, raging against them according to the one saying the prophet, 'I have envied with zeal for the Lord Pantokrator, whom the sons of Israel have forsaken' (1 Kings 19:10).

An evil man is a treacherous and deceiving man; but an unjust man is one who has ascended above this in wickedness, as if through craftiness and mischief, hastening the rational nature from virtue into wickedness, attempting to transfer it by some craft. Desiring to be saved from both, the one declaring the things set before him prays to God, since they reckoned iniquity against him, hiding it in their own heart, so that through remaining hidden, what such people are, they might be able to ensnare him, standing hostilely and against him for the sake of the duration of his life. Therefore, if it is said, 'All the day they prepared wars,' having no time of peace and rest, instead of a sword they have sharpened the tongue of themselves upon the deceiver, and being able to wound, they utter a word imitating the serpent who corrupts in his craftiness. And under their own lips, that is, their speech, they have thoughts made to be cast into them by evil powers because of the harmful and venomous nature of what are called 'darts.' And it is possible also concerning the devil and the other invisible enemies to grasp these things.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Power of Salvation and the Battle of the Mind
english: For a man is often called an evil one and an enemy, the devil. But also one serving his purpose may be called an antichrist. Ps 139:5,6: The hand of a sinner, the sinful practice, prays to be guarded from by God acting as a watchman. And besides this, it is worthy that he also be rescued from men who intend to do wrong by their choice, since they have reasoned through deceptive words and thoughts to trip up the steps of those walking toward progress in greater things.

It is possible in these things to catch the sinner, the devil, and unjust men, or rather his evil angels, or those who work men toward iniquity of soul. For they possess a deceptive wisdom, which they do not bring forth openly but hide like a snare under their sophistical words. But also their complex ropes of wickedness, which are composed and entwined by their sophistical words, stretch out to catch the feet of those walking rightly, calculating through these ropes to trip the steps of those who unthinkingly follow a path that someone has worn down.

Obstacles and stumbling blocks are, if they are thoughts, being cast against those intending to walk well and according to virtue. But he who has known himself, that he is not self-sufficient to remain harmless before so many [dangers], flees to God and requires power; therefore he also announces those surrounding him. Ps 139:7,8: He who is mastered by practice and thought will say practically to Him, 'My God, are you?' and it is worthy that he asks how his voice of petition might be heard, receiving it unto his own. For he truly says, 'O Lord of all, and You are my Lord, and I am your servant; therefore You are the power of my salvation.' For of the truly and attainable salvation of yours, man's power exists to have an impossible salvation if he has not become in you. And my salvation is the likeness according to the image and the likeness that has become yours, to partake of your holiness through which also salvation exists. And that very gospel is the power of God unto salvation, as it is written by the apostle regarding the one becoming in the gospel...

One possesses the power of salvation by living and acting according to the Gospel. The power of my salvation, O Lord, has overshadowed my head on a day of war, specifically my mental head. I am convinced, therefore, that nothing is difficult against the invisible enemies during the day, that is, during the temporal extension of this life. The testimony that the head is mental is found in 'The blessing of the Lord is upon the head of the righteous' (Ps 112:3) and 'The eyes of the wise are in his head' (Ps 111:10).

The sinful devil takes those who perform sin, making them his instruments. It is not clear, however, if one is mastered by a certain shameful desire. For if someone is drawn from desire into practical sin, he immediately becomes the devil's instrument; but if, having looked at a woman with desire, one stops in thought to prevent the fulfillment of the desires, he will not become the intended sinner. Therefore, one prays to the Lord that from desire alone, without being drawn into the action of the desire, he may not be handed over to the sinner, nor proceed further being conquered by it, but rather always be prevented by the better thought from You. It is also said: since all good desire is present to me as a righteous man, let me not be such as to fall from such desire and be handed over to the sinner having acted sinfully.

‘Lest through many of my thoughts I may be able to [sin], do not leave me, guarding me in the shelter of your wings and under your strong hand’ (Ps 139:23-24), so that no one may seize or lift himself up arrogantly against me as one caught by him. A fighter and a slanderer is one who is accustomed to speaking with a wagging tongue. For no one of such a kind is able to be directed in a good disposition, always turning away from the fighter; for they are lovers of sinning through rejoicing in battles, insults, and slanders. Therefore, it is not possible for such a person to be directed by virtue. And he who is always trivial in everything is called unrighteous. Perhaps he speaks of the hand that operates the corruption in those who frequently perform many evil deeds.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Sacrifice of Praise and the Discipline of Silence
english: Punishment is corruption, appearing from the corruption. 'With your corruption, O Jerusalem, who will help?' (Ps 79:9). And also the hand-operated disposition will be corrupted because of uncleanness; it will be corrupted by decay, as it is shown by 'Evil conversations corrupt good habits' (Ps 139:13-14).

He says 'judgment' is the examination of deeds and intentions, and 'justice' is the repayment according to merit. And even if the same subject is signified by both words in a parallel way, examine it yourself. The same must be said concerning the poor and the needy; for indeed, both names applied to the same thing must be taken according to different matters, such as being 'poor' if one has fallen greatly from wealth (for the rich have become poor and hungry), but 'needy' being one who has the necessary things for living through toil rather than through property.

The righteous confess either that they have not fallen into such things themselves, or that those who disregarded them and caused them much harm were subjected to such burdens by the judgment and justice of God. Regarding the confession of the righteous, the upright—others of the righteous—will dwell in the face of the Lord; those who confessed by the name, the righteous, confessed. Others of the righteous, the upright, if not entirely in substance, but in thought only, being righteous in one who performs moral virtues, and upright in one who has possessed the contemplation of truth.

Perhaps one who sometimes performs praiseworthy things may be called righteous, but while the practical man of the righteous confesses by the name of God, the upright one has acquired a city and a house through contemplation, dwelling in the face of God. For the character of the substance has been shown to be the face of God, Him dwelling in this face, concerning which it is said everywhere, 'If anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation' (2 Cor 5:17).

And if the 'upright who will dwell with your face' is to be explained, not thus: 'that your face they will dwell in, the upright, not going out from the face of the Lord God like Cain (Gen 4:16), or fleeing from it according to those things said concerning him, "And Adam and his wife fled from the face of the Lord God" (Gen 3:8).' But not thus: 'You are found upright, saving the image and likeness of you, having become conformed...'

They dwell in the likeness of the image of your Son, so that your Son may be found [in them], the fulfillment of what the Savior said concerning such things: 'I am that I am, and they shall be with me, to behold my glory.' And this is to be heard not locally but in a God-befitting manner.

[Ps 140:2b] This sacrifice is offered by one who, having hurried to complete it, reaches the evening, while the one sacrificing in the morning offers according to the law the sacrifices that present the sensible things. But at noon, after this, he who has learned what is said by the Lord, 'You desire sacrifice, not burnt offerings, but the knowledge of God' [Ps 140:3]. And above all, an evening sacrifice is to be heard, the offering of the hands previously mentioned.

[Ps 140:3-4] If the lips of the prophet approach with crushing, and a smooth-tongued man will not be directed upon the earth. May I also not fall into these things, O Lord; a guard to my mouth and a door of restraint around my lips. For I have set all things upon myself, having obeyed the exhortation of the one saying, 'With your words make a weight and a balance' [Prov 16:11]. For it is not advantageous for all to speak, nor even to be silent; for to the one able to open the mouth with the word of God, silence is not fitting, but to the one who brings forth a word that is idle and to those condemning words, silence will be for good. But those who practice silence differ from the one saying, 'He who keeps silence is found wise,' and 'He is keeping silence, for he has no answer,' and 'He is keeping silence, knowing the time.' For the one possessing the knowledge of the time to speak and the time when it is not necessary to speak, would ask that a guard and a door be present to his mouth and his lips from God, so that he might not bring forth anything unseasonably; and let the one who is not called to answer the questions being put forward be requested [to remain silent], so that, having been shown to be unbridled toward God, he might not answer rashly instead of others; for indeed, let the one found wise through silence seek confirmation from God by that silence through which he is found wise. And since men who work iniquity make excuses, defending themselves ostensibly on behalf of those on whose behalf they work wickedly, I, having entreated you much, O Lord, deserve [to be heard], that I might also [entreat] on behalf of not coming into such a disposition, or of having a heart flowing into words of wickedness upon the...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
